item.title: The Duskbloods Delayed to 2027 Due to Gameplay and Balance Adjustments
item.description:
The Duskbloods has been delayed to 2027. Learn more about the announcement here.

The Duskbloods Launch Window Moved to 2027


To Further Enhance Core Concepts, FromSoftware Says


The Duskbloods has been delayed from its planned 2026 release window to 2027. FromSoftware announced the news on X (Twitter) on October 29. According to the studio's post, "During the network test, we saw active interest in the core concepts of the game, including combat, strategic depth, and player expression." They added that the extra time would allow "final adjustments to game rules and balancing."
We'll update this article as more information becomes available. In the meantime, check out our article below for the latest on the game's release.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Casts Sonic VA Roger Craig Smith as Protagonist Soul
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero adds veteran voice actor Roger Craig Smith, who portrayed iconic gaming characters like Sonic, Chris Redfield, and Kyle Crane, to its English dub. Find out more details about Smith and his co-star Donnie Yen.

Sonic VA Roger Craig Smith Joins Phantom Blade Zero’s English Cast


Smith Replaces Original VA Jay Maksenuk Before Launch


Phantom Blade Zero has added veteran voice actor Roger Craig Smith to its final cast as Soul, the main protagonist and former elite assassin. Smith is best known for his longtime performance of Sonic the Hedgehog, first taking over the role in 2010 in Sonic Free Riders and Sonic Colors, and lending his voice to the character in most mainline games including 2024's Sonic x Shadow Generations. He also voiced the speedster in the animated series Sonic Boom and Disney's Wreck-it Ralph movies. Notably, he didn't reprise his role for the live-action films, as actor and comedian Ben Schwartz took over that portrayal.
Aside from Sonic, Smith has voiced several other major video game characters, including Ezio Auditore in Assassin’s Creed, Batman in Arkham Origins, Kyle Crane in Dying Light, and Mirage in Apex Legends. He began voicing Chris Redfield in 2009’s Resident Evil 5 and reprised the role in several games through Resident Evil 6. Capcom has yet to announce who will voice Chris in Code Veronica's remake, leaving it unclear whether Smith will return or the role will go to David Vaughn or Jeff Schine, who voiced Chris in Resident Evil 7 and Village, respectively.
Before Smith's last-minute casting was discovered, Jay Maksenuk had been the voice Soul, with his performance heard in earlier trailers and preview footage. Maksenuk, best known as V in Once Human and Gideon in Love and Deepspace, has now been replaced for the final release, though developer S-GAME has not explained why.

English and Chinese Voice Tracks Available On Launch


Donnie Yen Involved Personally as Creative Consultant


Smith joins Donnie Yen (star of the Ip Man series), who portrays Mó Yuan, the father of protagonist Soul and leader of the Bastion of Mó. Yen supplied his likeness, facial performance, and full-body motion capture for the character, and recorded his dialogue. The Hong Kong action star has also served as the game’s creative consultant since 2023, helping shape its kung fu punk wuxia style and action design.
Yen’s involvement extended beyond his own performance, showing that he's all-in on the project. According to RPG Gamer's coverage of S-GAMES' Q&A, he brought members of his stunt team into the motion-capture process and helped refine Mó Yuan’s portrayal as a father, which special care and attention for the flow, aesthetics, and philosophy of the combat.
Early reviews have praised the game’s performance capture and synchronized English and Chinese voice tracks, although reactions to individual English performances have varied. Players will be able to hear Smith alongside the rest of the English cast by selecting the English voice track in the game’s audio settings.
Phantom Blade Zero launches on October 29, 2026, for PS5 and PC. Physical discs will also be included in 2027. For more about the game, read our review of S-GAME’s self-described "kungfupunk" action RPG.
Source:
Phantom Blade Zero State of Play dives deep into combat and the Wulin world
Phantom Blade Zero Preview Q&A

item.title: Palworld Switch 2 Release Is Possible as Pocketpair CEO Says "We'd Love to Have Those Conversations"
item.description:
Palworld developer Pocketpair is open to bringing the game to Nintendo Switch 2. Read on to learn more about what CEO Takuro Mizobe said here.

Pocketpair CEO Open to Palworld on Nintendo Switch 2


Studio Would Welcome Talks to Bring Game on Nintendo Platforms


Palworld’s CEO Takuro Mizobe said that Pocketpair would be interested in discussing a Switch 2 version of Palworld. Asked in a recent interview on October 27th about his earlier comments that the console seemed like a great fit for the game, Mizobe called the Switch 2 an "amazing platform," especially for Japan and its game industry.
If the chance ever arises to consider a Switch release, he told VGC, "we'd love to have those conversations." For now though, no Switch version has been confirmed to be in the works.
Pocketpair has actually been interested in the idea of Palworld making it to the Nintendo consoles for sometime now. John "Bucky" Buckley mentioned if the Switch 2 was "beefy enough," the platform would be up for major consideration. The thought came at a time when the Nintendo Switch 2 was still unreleased and the full specs were unknown. Now that time has passed since the release of Palworld's 1.0 and a year after the Switch 2’s release, the studio has publicly confirmed they’d be open to the idea.
The team has already optimized specs for the Steam Deck, but they’d definitely look forward to adding the game to "more handhelds if possible." Still, this may likely remain unforeseeable until Pocketpair and Nintendo’s ongoing legal concerns get resolved. The case has since been reported to have narrowed to older versions of the game, and Palworld 1.0 still launched without restrictions.

Pocketpair Will Keep on Experimenting


Console exploration aside, Mizobe mentioned in the same interview that Pocketpair plans to keep supporting Palworld in myriad ways. As it’s growing into a broader IP, they’ve gained partners like Bushiroad for the recently released Palworld trading card game, though at the same time the team won’t be putting all their resources into it.
He wants Pocketpair to keep experimenting with new ideas and mixing genres, which he says can also bring Palworld to "new audiences," and he still considers Pocketpair as an indie studio despite the exponential growth. Upcoming titles like Palworld Online, Palworld! ~More Than Just Pals~, and Palworld: Palfarm are just a few of the spinoffs that they’re currently working on, but it goes to show that they’re making moves to expand their IP through various styles that are worth giving a try.
Sources:
Pocketpair CEO on keeping the indie spirit alive after Palworld's success
Nintendo and The Pokémon Company update Palworld lawsuit, limited to older versions only
Palworld Could Come To Switch 2 If The System Is “Beefy Enough”

item.title: Pokémon UNITE’s End of Service Coming in 2027, and Players Are Disappointed
item.description:
Pokémon UNITE will end service in March 2027, on both Nintendo Switch and mobile. Read on to learn more about the game’s shutdown and other details here.

Pokémon UNITE Confirmed To Shut Down in March 2027


Officially Reaching End of Service


The official Pokémon UNITE account has announced that the game will end service on March 23, 2027, at 00:00 UTC (March 22 at 5 PM PT / 8 PM ET), across all platforms. The game first launched on Switch on July 21, 2021, and the team has thanked players for their support since then. After the shutdown, players will no longer be able to log in or take part in battles, and support for the game's video and image guidelines will end as well.
The wind-down has already begun, with gacha currency sales, new UNITE Club memberships, and automatic membership renewals being suspended on October 27 at 05:00 UTC. Players can keep using the Aeos gems they currently own until service ends, including current UNITE Club members who keep their benefits until their membership period runs out.

Planned Events Are Still Scheduled To Arrive


Other planned game updates will still happen. On November 12, an update is set to add a special event and a "library" feature. During the event, players can earn various items and rewards, including Unite licenses and Holowear that have appeared in the game so far. Meanwhile, the library lets players view certain records and in-game content even after the game shuts down, but only if they complete the required data download before March 23, 2027.
Library data generally cannot be transferred between devices, and support for this feature ends once the game closes. Players must accomplish the data download, or they won’t be able to view their in-game records anymore afterwards. Additionally, the Pokémon UNITE Aeos Crown 2027 Tokyo competitive tournament will still take place as previously announced, with qualifiers starting on December 5, 2026.

Players Express Their Frustrations


Reactions to the official announcement have been negative, with some expecting it and many players voicing frustration over the game's end. A common point raised was that the developers didn’t listen to community feedback about monetization issues and instances where bots enter matches. There were also complaints in survey responses and suggestions from both players and content creators. Several fans criticized TiMi directly, saying the game's popular IP and genre should’ve allowed it to last longer.
Others expressed sadness at the news, particularly players who had spent money on the game and enjoyed it. Some felt that the game's issues could have been addressed earlier and that the shutdown was avoidable, though some pointed to its dwindling presence in the MOBA market as another factor. For now, the official notice encourages players to keep enjoying the game until its final day.
Sources:
Pokémon UNITE Official X Post
Pokémon UNITE End of Service (Official US Site)

GTA 6 developer and publisher Rockstar Games began shipping out the Grand Theft Auto VI Merch Collection on October 9, 2026. Take a look at the complete list of the available merchandise, including upcoming items available for pre-order.

Rockstar Games Now Shipping Out Vibrant Vice City-Themed Collectibles


The Grand Theft Auto VI Merch Collection Is Available for Purchase


Grand Theft Auto VI continues to drum up even more excitement among the gaming community as it speeds toward its much-awaited release. item.title: Aniimo Hits 160k Concurrent Players on Steam, Also Now Available on Mobile
item.description:
Aniimo surpasses 160,000 peak concurrent Steam players as its mobile version officially launches worldwide.

Aniimo Surpasses 160K Steam Players Alongside Mobile Launch’s Debut


Landed in Steam's Global Top 10 Sellers Chart


Aniimo, an open-world monster-collecting RPG by Pawprint Interactive Entertainment, has broken onto Steam's Global Top Sellers chart afterits mobile version officially launched on September 23, 2026, following its PC and console debut the week prior. According to SteamDB, concurrent players have climbed past 168,000, continuing a streak of daily records since its release on September 16.
To highlight the milestone, the developers sent players a Sparkling Egg reward, which has a Sparkling variant Aniimo, to their in-game mailbox as a thank-you, with more celebrations teased for the future.
In Aniimo, players get to explore the continent of Idyll while capturing and raising over 200 different creatures called Aniimo. The core mechanic lets players "twin" with their Animo to borrow their abilities for traversal, puzzle-solving, combat, and more. The mobile version carries over the same features as its PC and console counterparts, with full cross-play and cross-save support across all platforms.

Mobile Gets Slight Delays with Players Being Compensated


The mobile release did hit a short delay, lasting roughly less than an hour, as Aniimo's official X (Twitter) account announced that service would be pushed back to ensure the quality of the update. Servers eventually went live shortly after, and the team confirmed a compensation package of 1000 Glimmers, the game’s premium currency, a total of the original maintenance and the added delay, along with a Sparkling Cube, for catching Aniimo.
Since the in-game mailbox was temporarily unavailable at the time, the developers said the rewards would arrive in two separate mails once said function was restored.
Aniimo is free-to-play with in-game purchases and is available now on PC via Steam and Epic Games Store, PlayStation 5, Xbox Series X|S, iOS, and Android. For more insights on the game, check out the article below!

item.title: Aniimo Spotlights Unique Creature Design and Hand-Drawn Animations Each in Behind-The-Scenes Showcase
item.description:
Aniimo developer Pawprint Studio shared new details on the creative vision behind the upcoming open-world RPG. Learn more about the design process for the continent of Idyll and how fans are reacting to the new developer showcase.

Aniimo Developer Details the Creation of Idyll in Behind-the-Scenes Showcase


Pawprint Studio Explores the Journey From Concept to Reality


Aniimo developer Pawprint Studio has released an official behind-the-scenes documentary, giving players a closer look at the creative endeavor required to bring the upcoming free-to-play, next-gen creature-catching action RPG to life ahead of its September 16th launch.
The showcase highlights the development team's journey of turning abstract concepts into the continent of Idyll. Focusing heavily on world-building and creature design, the documentary emphasizes the studio's goal to make every creature feel integrated into a living environment where players can forge new bonds. Behind-the-scenes clips reveal contributions across different departments, including environment design, character modeling, and animation, with animators noting that each creature features a massive suite of hand-keyframed animations to ensure high fidelity.

Hand-Crafted Creature Animations Take Center Stage


A major highlight of the video is the deep dive into the painstaking effort required to bring the world's wildlife to life. Highlighting the massive scale of production behind the project, Tengfei, a model designer, explained that materials used for Aniimo still follow real-world laws of physics, but are refined, elevated, and reimagined for the game. He stated, "Take the Nimbi for example. A real sheep might have realistic fur or curly wool. But the Nimbi incorporates the characteristics of clouds, so we need to blend wool-like and cloud-like materials."
The development team also noted that creatures are designed around their distinct body features and natural personality traits rather than solely focusing on conventional cuteness. This approach shines through in playful additions like Nimbi, a fluffy teal-peach cloud creature, and Reefish, the quirky aquatic Aniimo with a blobfish-like design. They stand alongside other standout roster entries like Bouldus, the rugged rock-rolling Aniimo; Magmarex, the imposing fiery reptilian brute; and the graceful butterfly Aniimo, Gracewing.
Each and every Aniimo is made with care, down to its unique, handmade animations. Animator Lu Kun shared that "all of them [the animations] are manually keyframed," despite the massive effort it would take. Each individual Aniimo has about at least 100 animations, all tailored to that specific creature—"we never reuse animations across different Aniimo," he clarified.
Ayu, another co-animator, added that the team considered using motion capture for efficiency but ultimately decided against it in favor of creating a fun, imaginative world.
"Why do we put in so much effort? Why spend so much time on things that might seem they're not worth the trouble? There's only one goal: to create this world. To make it feel more alive and authentic. That's a world that truly feels like it's living and breathing," she concluded.

Fans Appreciate Developer Transparency and Teased Creatures


The behind-the-scenes video has sparked positive engagement across community hubs like Reddit and X. Fans have expressed genuine appreciation for seeing the real people behind the project, noting that transparent developer insights build strong confidence ahead of launch.
Additionally, community discussions quickly zeroed in on the highlighted creature concepts featured in the video, with fan favorites like Reefish and Nimbi quickly generating widespread excitement among creature-collector veterans.

item.title: Aniimo Release Date Confirmed For September 15 On Its PlayStation Page
item.description:
Aniimo, the upcoming free-to-play creature-catching open-world title, confirms a September release date through its PlayStation store page.

Aniimo PlayStation Storefront Reveals Release Date


To Launch on September 15th


Aniimo’s launch date comes earlier than expected, set for release on September 15, 2026, as revealed by their PlayStation store page. While there is no official announcement yet on any of Aniimo’s social media accounts as of writing, the PlayStation Store front clearly notes that it will be releasing simultaneously in all regions on September 15th or 16th, depending on location, with the bottom description also writing that "Aniimo will officially launch as a free-to-play title on September 16, 2026 at 10:00 (UTC+8). This means the base game offered through this pre-order campaign will be available at no cost."
Refer to the table below for when it will release in the following regions:

BrazilTuesday, September 15, 2026, 11:00 p.m.
Universal Time (UTC)Wednesday, September 16, 2026, 2:00 a.m.

Unexpected Release Date "Announcement"


The sneaky release date notice comes as a welcome surprise, as Aniimo had just finished its Global Closed Beta test in July and is gearing up for an appearance in the upcoming Gamescom Opening Night Live on August 25th. The pinned post on their official X (Twitter) also hints that they have "something exciting" to share with the fans during the event, suggesting a grand release date announcement in one of this year’s biggest gaming conventions.
They appear to be going all in with their participation, as their Gamescom booth is fully decked out with activities, such as hands-on gameplay, special guest appearances, and massive giveaways that range from exclusive Aniimo merchandise, such as plush toys and badges, to heavyweight prizes like an Alienware Aurora 16 Gaming Laptop, an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080, and custom Xbox Controllers.
Nevertheless, eagle-eyed fans who spotted the supposed release date shared their excitement over on X (Twitter) and Reddit, excited to finally dip their toes into the world of Idyll for themselves. Although, some have also lamented that it comes out the same day as Marvel’s Wolverine, alongside other highly anticipated September releases such as The Blood of Dawnwalker, Control Resonant, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, to name a few, fearful that it will take away the spotlight from the more "cozy-looking" title.
Despite that, a lot of cozy gamers have poured out words of support and anticipation for the upcoming creature-collecting game on social media. Others have praised the game even at the Closed Beta Test phase for its visuals and engaging gameplay, setting expectations for a solid launch.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Launch Trailer Confirms 2027 Physical Disc Release
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero releases its official launch trailer with digital pre-load dates and news of a 2027 physical release. Read on to learn more about the launch and other information.

Phantom Blade Zero Gears Up for Digital Launch With Physical PS5 Release Set for 2027


Pre-Load Dates and Physical Editions Confirmed Alongside Launch Trailer


Developer S-GAME has released the launch trailer for Phantom Blade Zero, confirming its digital rollout dates and PS5 physical editions that will arrive sometime in 2027. Pre-load opens on October 26 at 7 PM PT / 10 PM ET (October 27 at 10 AM Beijing Time), giving players a chance to download the game ahead of its official launch on October 28 at 7 PM PT / 10 PM ET (October 29 at 10 AM Beijing Time). The game launches digitally on PS5 and PC through Steam and the Epic Games Store.
The physical release will come in Standard, Deluxe, and Ultimate editions for PS5, though an exact month has yet to be announced. Fans reacted with excitement to the news, with many hoping to pick up a copy once it becomes available.

Combat and World Exploration Featured


Set in the Phantom World, Phantom Blade Zero blends traditional Chinese Wuxia lore with steampunk and mechanical prosthetics to form its Kungfupunk aesthetic. As highlighted in our Phantom Blade Zero Hands-On Preview, players step into the shoes of Soul, an elite assassin framed for his master's death with only 66 days left to live. Combat is fluid and fast-paced, pairing dual-blade combos with secondary Phantom Edges such as hand cannons and heavy axes that can break enemy guards and open up traversal paths.
The game puts a strong focus on action-movie choreography. In our Phantom Blade Zero Developer Interview, Director Qiwei Soulframe Liang shared how the team worked with martial arts masters on motion capture to achieve authentic, high-speed combat. Players can also expect more than 30 weapons and over 20 Phantom Edges to experiment with across the world of Wulin, along with more than 50 bosses in its semi-open world.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero's Deep Dive Reveals A 66 Day Permadeath Mode
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero's State of Play dove into combat, weapons, and Donnie Yen's role, but 66 Days mode stands out most, turning Soul's in-story death sentence into an actual permadeath difficulty option.

Kung Fu, Countdown, and a Killer New Difficulty Mode


66 Days Mode Makes Soul's Countdown Permanent


Phantom Blade Zero, the upcoming action RPG from Chinese developer S-Game, finally got its own dedicated State of Play on August 17, delivering on a promise founder and CEO Soulframe Liang made back in June. When Liang pushed the game's release date back roughly 50 days, from September 9 to October 29, he told fans in a post on X that once pre-orders opened, a State of Play devoted entirely to Phantom Blade Zero would follow: a focused dive into the game's world, combat, exploration, and progression systems, with nearly everything shown being new. This week's broadcast made good on that, covering combat, weapons, and martial arts star Donnie Yen's role in Soul's story, alongside a new permadeath difficulty option called 66 Days mode.
Despite early gameplay drawing comparisons to Soulslike titles like Elden Ring, Liang has pushed back on that label directly, describing the game in a June 2025 developer letter as closer to what he's coined "Wuxia Action," blending fast-paced martial arts combat with the cinematic, historically rooted storytelling of classic kung fu and wuxia films.
The story centers on Soul, the game's protagonist, who's been framed for his master's murder, betrayed by his own blood brother, and left alive only through a mysterious healer's intervention, one that comes with a fatal condition giving him just 66 days to live. Per the game's latest State of Play deep dive, that number isn't just a story detail. It's also the name of the game's hardest optional difficulty mode, and it plays exactly as bluntly as it sounds: every death costs the player time, and if that 66-day clock hits zero, the run ends in permanent death.
That's a meaningfully different pitch than the genre's usual difficulty options, which tend to just scale enemy damage or aggression up or down. The 66 Days mode instead ties Soul's fictional mortality directly to a mechanical stopwatch, turning every fight into a resource and raising the stakes of failure compared to a simple "load last checkpoint." Since the Soulslike genre is partly based on players choosing to play a challenging game, a built-in, narrative permadeath mode is the kind of feature that tends to generate exactly the bragging rights and clip-sharing conversations developers hope for.
However, it's not the only difficulty option on offer. According to the PlayStation Blog post, written by S-Game founder and CEO Soulframe Liang, Wayfarer mode is built for players who want to focus on the story with a more forgiving, cinematic combat experience. Meanwhile, the Hellwalker mode revolves around enemy AI that, according to the deep dive video, reacts to spacing, punishes whiffed attacks, and adapts to a player's habits instead of using fixed patterns.

The Wulin Setting Borrows Its Stakes From Wuxia Fiction


The PlayStation Blog post describes Phantom Blade Zero's setting as the Wulin, calling it "a place rife with conflict and intrigue" where Soul crosses paths with citizens caught up in the wider conspiracy around him. That word choice is doing more work than it might look like. In wuxia fiction, the Wulin (sometimes rendered Jianghu) isn't a physical kingdom with borders on a map; it's the shadow society of martial artists, sects, assassins, and wandering swordsmen who operate by their own code, largely outside the reach of formal law.
Decades of wuxia novels and films have used that setting specifically because it lets betrayal, honor, and vengeance play out with real consequences: there's no king to appeal to and no court to settle a grudge, only reputation and the blade. That's the tradition Phantom Blade Zero is explicitly drawing from, and it's worth knowing going in, because it reframes Soul's 66-day death sentence less as a video-game gimmick and more as a plot device lifted straight from the genre's own playbook, where a ticking clock or a poisoned body is a classic setup for a hero who has nothing left to lose.
It also explains why S-Game keeps stressing that the world is handcrafted rather than procedurally sprawling. A Wulin built for wandering swordsmen works best as a series of dangerous, distinct territories, each with its own factions and grudges, rather than one seamless open map; the structure supports the kind of story Liang says he's telling.

Combat Features More Than 30 Weapons and Reforgeable Builds


Outside of its difficulty options, the deep dive spent significant time on Phantom Blade Zero's weapon and build systems. Per the PlayStation Blog, players will unlock more than 30 primary weapons over the course of the game, alongside 25 secondary weapons called Phantom Edges, with named examples shown in the deep dive including the Drunken Sword Style, the twin-bladed White Serpent and Crimson Viper, the Soft Snake sword, and the Tiger Cannon.
Weapons can be upgraded and paired with accessories to build a specific combat style, whether that means favoring ranged options, calling in summons for assistance, or leaning into a specific weapon's unique techniques, which the deep dive noted gets unlocked as that weapon is upgraded rather than being available from the start.
To keep that experimentation low-risk, the game includes a Reforging Talisman, which lets players fully reset a weapon's upgrade level and recover the materials spent on it to reinvest elsewhere, addressing a common frustration in build-heavy action RPGs where players feel locked into early upgrade decisions. The PlayStation Blog also noted that some enemies expand the player's available arsenal when defeated, tying weapon progression directly into combat encounters rather than separating it out into crafting or shop systems.

A Publicly Tested Combat System


S-Game didn't wait until this week's broadcast to put Phantom Blade Zero's combat in front of players, though this was the most detailed public look at it to date. Per Notebookcheck's reporting, content creators including YouTuber Punish got hands-on time with a 60-minute playable build at a two-day S-Party event in Beijing back in July 2025, followed by a 500-square-meter, 60-station booth at Gamescom 2025 in Cologne that August, with additional showcases at ChinaJoy and Tokyo Game Show the same year.
That's a notably long public testing runway for an action RPG built around precise parrying and stance-switching. It also lines up with the roughly 50-day delay S-Game announced this past June: rather than a rushed, last-minute schedule slip, the extra development time capped off more than a year of the studio putting the combat system in front of real players at conventions and adjusting based on what didn't land.

Donnie Yen Plays Both Consultant and Character


Martial arts star Donnie Yen, known to Western audiences for the Ip Man series, Rogue One: A Star Wars Story, and John Wick: Chapter 4, serves as Phantom Blade Zero's Creative Consultant while also providing facial and motion capture for Mó Yuan, a martial arts master, per the PlayStation Blog post. It's a role that goes beyond a typical celebrity cameo: Yen built his reputation over decades in Hong Kong action cinema as both a performer and an action choreographer, and Liang described the collaboration as central to the game's authenticity, crediting Yen's involvement with helping translate real kung fu cinema technique into the game's combat rather than treating it as a licensing exercise.
According to an earlier PlayStation Blog post announcing the State of Play itself, Yen has held the Creative Consultant role since 2023, meaning his input has shaped the combat system since well before this week's broadcast rather than being brought on late for marketing purposes. That dual background, performer and choreographer, is precisely why his "Creative Consultant" credit here means something different than a typical celebrity tie-in: it's the same skill set S-Game needs to make Soul's swordplay read as authentic technique rather than stylized button-mashing, and it maps directly onto the "Wuxia Action" label Liang has used to describe the game since mid-2025.

A Delayed Release Now Locked to October 29, With a Console Exclusivity Window


All that groundwork, from Yen's involvement to years of convention testing, is finally coming together for players on a set date. Phantom Blade Zero releases October 29, 2026, on PS5 and PC via Steam and the Epic Games Store, day and date across all three storefronts. That date is itself a change worth knowing about: according to the official Phantom Blade Zero account, the game was originally set to launch September 9, 2026, a date S-Game had deliberately chosen to symbolically mirror Soul's own reversal of fate.
In June, Liang announced a roughly 50-day delay to October 29, apologizing directly to the community and describing the decision as necessary to give the game "one step further" before release, rather than ship it with room left for improvement. According to a post on the official Phantom Blade Zero X account, the extra time specifically went toward a final polish pass, including upgraded character models, reworked environments, and additional effort to preserve the game's visual quality for players who don't have ray tracing enabled.
Beyond the release date itself, platform access won't be equal at launch. Per a disclaimer shown at the end of the game's official release date announcement trailer, the PS5 version carries a 12-month console exclusivity window, meaning Xbox and Switch players won't have access to the game until at least October 2027, while the PC version isn't affected by that restriction. For players on PC specifically, the game is built on Unreal Engine 5 and will support Nvidia DLSS 4.5, including Super Resolution and Multi Frame Generation, alongside ray-traced reflections, shadows, and caustics, according to NVIDIA's own GeForce News post detailing the game's technical specs. On PS5, the PlayStation Blog confirmed support for adaptive triggers and 3D audio, tied into precision attacks and haptic feedback during combat.
Phantom Blade Zero also isn't as new an idea as its Unreal Engine 5 presentation might suggest. Per the PlayStation Blog, Liang wrote directly that the project traces back to Rainblood: Town of Death, a game he built solo using RPG Maker in 2010 while studying architecture, first in Beijing and then in New Haven. That project grew into the broader Phantom Blade franchise, primarily released on mobile in China, before Liang founded S-Game to eventually build what he's called "the spiritual rebirth of the original Rainblood" at a far larger scale for a global release. For more information on Phantom Blade Zero, including its full release date, platforms, and editions, check out the article below!

item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero is set for a dedicated State of Play with nearly 20 minutes of new gameplay and details about its combat, characters, and world. Find out what to expect from the presentation and the game's upcoming release below.

Phantom Blade Zero State of Play Will Show New Gameplay and Characters


Starts August 17 at 7:00 P.M. PT / 10:00 P.M. ET


Phantom Blade Zero will get its own dedicated State of Play presentation on August 17, with S-GAME set to show nearly 20 minutes of new gameplay for the upcoming action game. S-GAME will introduce several "never-before-seen characters central to our story," with the studio promising a more detailed look at what players can expect when the game launches on October 29, 2026. Donnie Yen Joins Phantom Blade Zero as Creative Consultant


The announcement comes alongside an 11-minute trailer that follows Soul through several new encounters. The footage shows him fighting enemies on a speeding wagon before facing The Hunt, one of his former comrades.
These scenes offer another look at the game's fast-paced sword combat, while the upcoming State of Play will provide more information about the systems behind it. S-GAME has specifically pointed to player builds as one of the subjects of the presentation, with the developer saying that players will have room to shape how Soul fights.
Phantom Blade Zero follows Soul, an assassin who survives an attempt on his life but is left with only 66 days to live. He must deal with the people responsible for the attack while uncovering a larger conspiracy. PlayStation describes the game as a fusion of classic wuxia storytelling and action, with Unreal Engine 5 powering its world and combat. The game takes place in the Phantom World, a setting that draws from the style of classic Hong Kong action films.
Donnie Yen has served as a creative consultant on Phantom Blade Zero since 2023. He has worked with S-GAME on the game's combat design and brought his "martial arts and action filmmaking expertise" to the project to help deliver an authentic kung fu experience, according to Liang. Members of Yen's stunt team have contributed to the production as well. Yen will provide the facial and motion-capture performance for Mó Yuan, Soul's father, who appears masked in the pre-order trailer as he gives Soul a beating.
Yen is best known for his work in martial arts movies, with roles in films such as Ip Man, Flash Point, and SPL: Sha Po Lang. He has also played Chirrut Îmwe in Rogue One: A Star Wars Story and portrayed Caine in John Wick: Chapter 4. His decades of experience as a martial artist, actor, and action choreographer have made him one of the most prominent figures in modern martial arts cinema.
S-GAME has described Phantom Blade Zero before as a "Kungfupunk" action game, with traditional wuxia elements mixed with "intricate machines reminiscent of steampunk." Previous footage has centered on its swordplay, which allows Soul to switch between different weapons and use a wide range of attacks against human and supernatural enemies. Liang said the presentation next week is expected to provide a much closer look at how these mechanics work.
Pre-orders for Phantom Blade Zero are now available on PS5. Players who pre-order will get early access to the Treasure Basin accessory and Legacy outfit, although both items can be unlocked through in-game progression after launch. The game is set to release on October 29, 2026.
Phantom Blade Zero was originally scheduled to launch on September 9, 2026, before S-GAME pushed the game back to October 29. The studio said the additional time will go toward polishing the game, with upgraded character models and reworked environments among the changes planned for release. The game's release will come nearly three years after its debut at the 2023 PlayStation Showcase, where S-GAME first introduced Soul and the Phantom World.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Skips Xbox at Launch, Timed PS5 & PC Exclusive
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero will be PC and PS5 exclusive for at least 12 months. Read on to learn more about which platforms the game will release on and what was showcased in its latest trailer.

Phantom Blade Zero Release Date Reveal At TGA 2025


PC and PS5 Exclusive For At Least Its First 12 Months


Phantom Blade Zero will launch on PC and PlayStation 5 in September 2026, and will remain exclusive on those platforms for its first year. As stated at the end of the release date reveal video at The Game Awards 2025, the game will not be available on other consoles for at least 12 months after release date.
This is the most common trend for major Sony-published PlayStation exclusives –initially launching exclusively to PlayStation consoles only, then on PC after a set period (usually 1–2 years), and rarely (if ever) released on other consoles like Xbox.
Titles like Final Fantasy XVI, Black Myth: Wukong, and Silent Hill 2 Remake all maintained PlayStation exclusivity for a year or more before their eventual release on Xbox. Although developer S-GAME has yet to confirm which platforms the game will release on beyond PC and PS5, many expect Phantom Blade Zero to also launch on Xbox Series X|S or Nintendo Switch 2.

The Phantom and The Blade


The latest trailer for Phantom Blade Zero not only revealed the game’s release date, but also gave more previews of the highly anticipated Wuxia action RPG. Running at over 4 minutes, the video showcased new bosses, gameplay, and the game’s narrative.
Starting off with protagonist Soul’s backstory, the trailer briefly explains that he is being hunted down by the Order. Within his adventures, he will meet various friends and foes that will play significant roles in his journey.
The trailer’s narration also harked on the game’s namesake, showing importance to the concept of the Phantom and the Blade. It stated, "Phantom is movement, striking from where none expected. Blade is breath which channel into steel turning any blade into a divine weapon."
In terms of gameplay, it showcased a "semi-open" world structure, moving away from linear corridors toward interconnected regions that encourage exploration. The combat remains the star of the show with its fast pace and motion that is heavily inspired by traditional Wuxia martial arts films.
The video also featured a wider variety of secondary weapons, including heavy maces and long-range spears, all of which integrate seamlessly into a "flow-based" parry system. Additionally, new boss fights such as a chained giant, a drunken masked samurai, a lion dancer, and more were showcased, highlighting their unique playstyles and grand visual effects.
With an official release date announced, fans are excited to experience a new high speed action game that is reminiscent of classic Chinese action films. Although often compared to Soulslikes with its dark aesthetic and daunting boss battles, Phantom Blade Zero looks to start the new wave of the Wuxia action genre.
Phantom Blade Zero is set to be released on September 9, 2026 on PlayStation 5 and PC. To stay up to date with the latest information about the game, check out our article below!

Phantom Blade Zero Release Date Reveal At The Game Awards 2025


The Lion Awakens on TGA 2025


Phantom Blade Zero, the highly anticipated Wuxia action game, is set to reveal its release date at the upcoming Game Awards 2025 (TGA). As announced by the TGA’s official Twitter (X) on December 7, the kungfu punk RPG will have its world premiere announcement live during the awards show.

The 20-second teaser then fades to black, before revealing that Phantom Blade Zero's release date will be announced during TGA 2025. This suggests that the reveal date announcement could also bring in new gameplay footage for the game, particularly the lion dancer boss battle.

First Revealed During PlayStation Showcase 2023


Phantom Blade Zero was first unveiled to the public during the PlayStation Showcase in May 2023. Developed by S-GAME, the project piqued the interest of many for its hyper-stylized "Kungfu-Punk" aesthetic, fast-paced action, and cinematic combat.
Following its reveal, the game was featured in several gaming events, including Summer Game Fest and Gamescom, allowing players to experience a glimpse of the action. item.title: Phantom Blade Zero is Not a Soulslike, But a Wuxia Action, Reiterates Director
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero aims to create a new Wuxia Action genre. Read on to learn more about how the game differs from Soulslikes and the three difficulty options it features.

Phantom Blade Zero IS NOT A SOULSLIKE


Director Defines New Genre As "Wuxia Action"


Phantom Blade Zero Director Soulframe reiterated that the game is not a Soulslike, but instead a new genre type he coined as "Wuxia Action." Phantom Blade Zero’s official Twitter (X) account posted a Developer’s Letter on June 24, where Soulframe addressed several questions from fans regarding the game.
He noted that when the game was first announced, people immediately considered it a Soulslike for its interconnected maps, hidden secrets, and checkpoints. After the demo was released, people referred to it as a hack-and-slash title, as it had a faster pace compared to typical Soulslikes.
Although the director acknowledged that categorizing Phantom Blade Zero into a genre helps fans distinguish it from other games and build a general expectation, he emphasized that it is neither a Soulslike nor any other traditional action game. Despite this, Soulframe took inspiration from games of those genres, which led them to what they have today.
Initially, the development team’s goal was to make a hack-and-slash game with a multi-layered map. What came out was what Soulframe described as "something that felt deeply familiar to us, yet is rarely seen or experienced in games." It was a mixture of Chinese martial arts, Western combat techniques, and Hollywood filmmaking, which he attributed to kung fu master Bruce Lee.
A similar feel was applied to the game, differentiating it from existing genres. Soulframe stated, "Broadly speaking, it falls under the category of ARPGs. But more specifically— maybe it could create a new identity that is Wuxia Action Games?" In this new genre, he stated that fans can experience high-speed action, deep historical connections, and iconic cinema moments
This was the primary reason why developer S-GAMES wanted to invite everyone to their exclusive hands-on demo in Beijing, China, on July 26-27. The upcoming demo will give fans a "clearer glimpse of the game’s core experience."

Difficulty Options Revealed


It was previously reported that Phantom Blade Zero will have difficulty options, further differentiating it from Soulslike games. Continuing the developer’s letter, Soulframe confirmed that there will be three difficulty settings, namely Gamechanger, Wayfarer, and Hellwaker.
The Gamechanger is the default difficulty level, offering a balanced playthrough and is great for beginners. Meanwhile, Wayfarer is the easiest mode designed for those with little to no experience in action games. Finally, Hellwalker is the hardest mode, only unlocked in New Game+. It pushes players’ skills to the limit, featuring smarter AI, reshuffled movesets, and entirely new moves.
S-GAMES plans to announce the game’s release date before 2025 ends, giving fans more things to look forward to for the "kungfupunk" experience. Phantom Blade Zero is set to release in Fall 2026 for PlayStation 5. To stay up to date with the latest information about the game, check out our article below!

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Playtime Estimated to be 20-30 Hours with Adjustable Difficulty
item.description:
Phantom Blade Zero reportedly will have four difficulty options, along with new information regarding its gameplay features. Read to learn more about the development of Phantom Blade Zero, and what to expect for the game this 2025.

Phantom Blade Zero Development Updates


Phantom Blade Zero Not A Soulslike, Features Four Difficulty Options


According to recent reports, Phantom Blade Zero will have four difficulty options namely: easy, ordinary, difficult, and extremely difficult. The game has been compared to Soulslikes by fans after its reveal in PlayStation Showcase 2023 due to its aesthetic and combat. Adding difficulty options pushes Phantom Blade Zero away from these comparisons since Soulslike games are notoriously keen on being extremely difficult and not having other difficulty options.
Phantom Blade Zero Game Director Soulframe already addressed this in an official tweet made after the game was featured in Summer Game Fest 2024. He wanted to stress that "making another soulslike" was never part of the plan. We want combo-driven, heart-pumping combat that is hectic, rewarding, and exhilarating."
The game drew comparisons to soulslike games with its dark-themed world and unique boss fights. Soulframe confirmed that the game took inspiration from soulslike games with its multi-layered maps, multiple approach paths, and hidden nooks and crevices, although according to him, "the similarities stop there." He previously described the game as "Ninja Gaiden Combat on a Souls Game Map", combining hack-and-slash gameplay with extended area exploration.

Gameplay Features With Over 30+ Weapons, 20-30 Hours of Playthrough, And More


Several other details about Phantom Blade Zero came out from the recent interviews. Players will have the option to choose from 30 primary weapons and 20 secondary weapons, each having its unique gameplay and effects in battle. The game reportedly will have around 20-30 hours of main story playthrough and an additional 20-30 hours worth of side content.
Boss fights will consist of at least two phases. If the player dies during the second phase of the boss fight, they can directly start the challenge from the second phase without having to fight the first phase again. A new game mode called "Li Wulin" is mentioned, where players can fight previously defeated bosses, which leads them to unlock new hidden bosses to conquer.
There is also apparently a mechanic that affects the ending of the game, although it remains unclear as to how it will affect the overall playthrough and how many alternate endings the game can have.

Phantom Blade Zero Year Of The Snake Gameplay Trailer


Phantom Blade Zero uploaded a "Year of the Snake Gameplay Trailer" that features Soul, the main protagonist of the game, fighting a boss called "Chief Disciple of The Seven Stars." After the boss fight, the trailer continued by featuring weapons that Soul can wield, which include "Weapon No.13 Soft Snake Sword", and "Weapon No.27 White Serpent and Crimson Viper."
Based on the trailer, the release date for Phantom Blade Zero will be announced in 2025. Phantom Blade Zero’s official Twitter (X) page also posted a video to commemorate the Lunar New Year. In the video, Soulframe mentioned that the team has many more exciting announcements lined up later this year, and they are preparing to reveal something fans have never seen before.
Phantom Blade Zero is currently in development for PlayStation 5 with plans to release on PC as well. There is no official release date announced for the game.

item.title: Phantom Blade Zero Devs Respond to "Nobody Needs Xbox" Misquote
item.description:
S-GAME has finally addressed the controversial statement made by an anonymous source at ChinaJoy 2024. Discover the details of the uproar and the Phantom Blade developers’ response.

S-GAME Responds to the Controversy


Nobody Needs Xbox, Media Outlets Say


S-GAME, the developers behind Phantom Blade Zero and Black Myth: Wukong, finally issued a statement on Twitter(X) addressing claims made by an anonymous source. Multiple media outlets in attendance at the ChinaJoy 2024 event last week reported on the alleged Phantom Bladed Zero developer who made controversial statements towards Xbox.
The studio issued a statement on Twitter(x), reaffirming their commitment to making the game widely available.
"These claimed statements do not represent S-GAME’s values or culture," the statement reads. "We believe in making our game accessible to everyone and have not ruled out any platforms for Phantom Blade Zero. We are hard at work on both the development and publishing fronts to ensure that as many players as possible can enjoy our game at release and in the future."
The controversy began with a statement from an anonymous source—who claims to be a developer on Phantom Blade Zero—published in a Chinese news outlet. Directly translated by fans, it reads "no one shows any interest in Xbox." The news spread, with outlets like Aroged reporting that Xbox is "a platform that does not find demand, especially in Asia." However, the situation escalated when Brazilian outlet Gameplay Cassi mistranslated the statement as "nobody needs this platform" when citing Aroged.
In their response, S-GAME did not explicitly confirm nor deny the authenticity of the anonymous source. However, there is some grain of truth in their claims. Xbox’s popularity in Asia significantly lags behind PlayStation and Nintendo. In Japan, for instance, Xbox Series X|S sales barely reached half a million units in over four years. In contrast, the PS5 sold a million units in 2021 alone.
There is also the issue of the platform's availability in most Asian countries. For example, in 2021, Southeast Asia lacked retail support for Xbox, with Singapore being the only place where consoles, games, and accessories are distributed. This forced retailers in other Southeast Asian countries to rely on overseas wholesalers for their Xbox inventory.
The controversy escalated with speculation of an exclusive deal between S-GAME and Sony. While the studio previously acknowledged receiving development and marketing support from Sony in a June 8 interview with a Chinese content creator, they have since denied rumors of an exclusive partnership. In their Summer 2024 Developer Update, S-GAME honed in on the fact that "in addition to PlayStation 5, we’re planning to release it to PC as well."
Although the studio has not confirmed an Xbox release, their recent response to the controversy leaves the door open for the possibility of the game coming to the said platform.

item.title: Blue Archive JP’s Publisher Switch to Nexon in January 2027 Brings Mixed Reactions
item.description:
Blue Archive's Japanese service is changing publishers, moving from Yostar to Nexon in January 2027. Read on to learn more about the transfer announcement and other details.

Blue Archive JP Switches Publisher From Yostar to Nexon, Earning Mixed Fan Reactions


Official Statement Made During Blue Archive JP’s Latest Livestream


It was officially announced on the October 25th Blue Archive livestream that the game’s JP publisher is switching from Yostar to Nexon in January 2027. Maintenance for the switch is set for January, with the detailed schedule to be announced sometime this November. Nexon Games remains the developer, and there are no planned changes to how the game is made.
According to community summaries of the livestream, Nexon ended the contract at its request, as the full handover of publishing rights will take about three months, and previously announced offline events will continue as planned. The Chinese version, on the other hand, is reportedly staying with Yostar.

Players Must Link and Transfer Their Accounts


Nexon says all account data, including Blue Gems, packages, and items, will carry over, but players need to meet some requirements. Accounts must be first linked to a Yostar ID and registered for the transfer before the maintenance starts, while guest accounts can't be moved. After the switch, players will log in with a Nexon account instead, and anyone whose existing Nexon account was made through X (Twitter) has to register again.
Each Nexon account can hold only one Blue Archive account, so players with several Yostar IDs will need separate accounts, and Nexon Points can't be used in the game. Personal details tied to a Yostar ID, such as name and address, won't be transferred, and Nexon's own terms and privacy policy will apply. The procedure page is expected in November.
Other services are affected too. The PC version and Yostar's charge center stay available only until the maintenance begins, with Nexon preparing a new PC environment and a web-based payment option. Serial codes should be used before then, and items will keep their expiry dates. After the switch, players will receive compensation, including 100 free recruitments, and announced collaborations, merchandise, and events, including the Blue Academy Fest on January 23 and 24, are still on the way.

Japanese and Global Players Weigh In Their Worries


Reactions have been mixed, and many replies from Japanese players are those of concern. Part of the worries stem from Nexon's reputation among the community, as Nexon is focused on different marketing strategies vs. Yostar in other gacha titles, as discussed on Reddit. While Yostar is very fan-centric in promoting a game, Nexon is regarded by the gacha fans as having a heavier focus on microtransactions and monetization as leading factors. Some are hoping that the quality would not lessen or drop when going through the transition.
Though Nexon Games already serves as the core developer in JP, Yostar was widely credited with establishing Blue Archive’s media and promotional efforts and budget, especially in Japan. Fans pointed to merchandise, songs, ASMR, ads in Tokyo, the online shop, offline events, and the Blue Archive radio show, all headed by Yostar. Some players also noted that there are noticeable gaps in promotions and marketing elsewhere compared to Japan, such as fewer offline events and collaborations, less content outside the game, and past translation errors.
Several fans asked Nexon to reconsider, a few hoped Yostar would return, and some fear for the game's long-term future. Others argue the change matters less than it seems. Nexon already develops the game and publishes it everywhere outside Japan and China, so some expect just a few in-game changes, and global players describe Nexon's publishing as steady, with occasional freebies and responses to feedback. A few hope that with this, Nexon could eventually bring Japan-only extras to other regions, though that remains speculation for now.
At this time, more answers are due in November, when Nexon plans to share the maintenance schedule, the account transfer procedure, and an interview video with Blue Archive's executive producer and Yostar's CEO. Nexon confirms its commitment to updating the game's stories and features hasn't changed ahead of the sixth anniversary on February 4, 2027.

item.title: Goddess of Victory: NIKKE 4th Anniversary Welcomes Stellar Blade Collab, new Marian, and Free SSR
item.description:
Goddess of Victory: NIKKE celebrates their 4th Anniversary with a Stellar Blade collaboration, new NIKKEs to recruit, and fan events.

NIKKE’s 4th Anniversary Introduces Stellar Blade Collab, New Characters, Free SSR


Marian, Scarlet, and Rapunzel Are the 4th Anniversary Stars


As revealed in today’s livestream, Goddess of Victory: NIKKE’s 4th Anniversary celebration comes in with plenty of new content, such as a Stellar Blade music collaboration, three new characters to add to the roster, and in-person fan celebrations.
Launching on October 29th, the 4th Anniversary update introduces Marian: Queen and Scarlet: Goddeath as recruitable NIKKEs, while Rapunzel: Sanctuary is a free SSR claimable up to four times through participating in anniversary events. Various in-game rewards will be available, with Commanders (NIKKE players) earning up to 259 free recruitment attempts during the duration of the event, with 4th Anniversary NIKKE selection boxes. These special selection boxes include:
  • Rapunzel: Sanctuary
  • Chime
  • Rapunzel: Pure Grace
  • Snow White: Innocent Days

Four new costumes also make their way to the game, two of which are obtained through gacha; Marian: Queen gets a “Last Affection” wedding dress costume where she “has attained happiness with her one true love,” while Snow White: Heavy Arms receives a “Lacrimosa” costume. Battle Pass costumes, Neon_Vision and Nayuta_Vision are also available on the update’s launch.
Stellar Blade, another popular action-adventure game from SHIFT UP, makes its way to the NIKKE universe with its second collaboration in the form of a soundtrack collection. Players can enjoy 22 tracks in TRACING THE STARS x Stellar Blade, added into the game with minigame backgrounds, custom note skins, and the special character appearance.

Plus a Main Story Expansion, Story Events, and a Visual Novel Adventure


The Main Story will receive an expansion, adding Main Chapters 49-50. As the full-scale 3rd Surface Recapture War is at hand, this finale chapter marks the end of the Underground Ark plotline while also setting down the foundation for a brand-new story about to unfold. Amidst that, players can also tune into the “MARIA-n” Story Event featuring Marian in an unfamiliar environment, taking steps towards discovering long hidden secrets.
Additionally, there will be a minigame called “Fading Affection,” a choice-driven text-based visual novel with branching storylines that gives players the chance to revisit memory fragments and discover unexplored endings of the past.

Taking Over Time Square Again Alongside In-Person Fan Events


NIKKE players in New York and Los Angeles can also take part in the in-person festivities. Alongside the update launch, a special NIKKE billboard on One Times Square (1475 Broadway & 42nd St.) will be on display for the entire day of October 29th. Eager fans can see Marian in action, taking over the heart of NYC, and take pictures with her.
For those in the West Coast, NIKKE will be featured in Animate Los Angeles in a special partnership for a “dedicated anniversary experience” that will feature plenty of photo displays such as the 3D illusion wall art and NIKKE-themed store decorations. Exclusive merchandise will also be on sale, and those who would stick around for a while longer can participate in special community activities. The NIKKE x Animate LA collaboration will run from October 31st to November 14th.

Spanish Language Support To Be Added


As part of NIKKE’s “growth around the globe,” the livestream also revealed that full Spanish text localization will be added to the game on October 29th.
“We are excited to welcome more Spanish-speaking players from the LATAM region with the addition of the much requested Spanish language support launching with the 4th Anniversary Update, and we will continue to do our best to deliver exciting content for all our players going forward,” said Hyongseok Yoo, VP of SHIFT UP and NIKKE’s Game Director, suggesting that with that initiative, more localizations may be in development.
Source:
Goddess of Victory: NIKKE Press Release
